props.name: yield high above/below 400 °C; satisfactory at 340-350 °C and >100 atm

evidence.quote: The yield remains fairly high even at temperatures exceeding 400° C. or somewhat lower. It is satisfactory at 340-350° C., and at pressures slightly higher than 100 atmo-

props.statement: The yield remains fairly high at temperatures above 400 °C or somewhat lower; it is satisfactory at 340-350 °C and at pressures slightly higher than 100 atmospheres.

props.statement: Certain grades of green smithsonite, containing ferrous carbonate isomorphous with the zinc carbonate, can be used advantageously for methanol synthesis without simultaneous formation of methane.

props.name: prior artificial catalysts need preparation, reduction, agglomerants; some expensive

evidence.quote: Some require careful prep- aration, and others have to undergo a reduc. tion treatment previous to being used.
many of the catalyzers proposed are very expensive, particularly those obtained by

props.statement: Proposed methanol catalysts are artificial, made by wet methods with filtration, washing, drying and agglomeration; some need careful preparation or reduction before use, some are diluted by inert carriers or need agglomerants, and many are expensive (rare-metal activants such as uranium, thorium, cobalt).

props.name: impurities in catalysts may give methane instead of alcohols

evidence.quote: in relatively small quantity in the catalyzers, may radically alter the course of the synthe- sis; they may, for example, produce methane instead of alcohols.

props.statement: Certain impurities, even in relatively small quantity in the catalysts, may radically alter the course of the synthesis, e.g. producing methane instead of alcohols.

props.statement: The raw crystalline mineral, despite coloured parts and foreign matter (iron, manganese, lime, silica), can after rough breaking be put directly into the catalysing towers; preheated to close to 400 °C it is ready for the synthesis.

props.name: smithsonite enormously more active than Zn/Cr carbonate or oxide

evidence.quote: perature and gas velocity, mineral smithson- Ite has an enormously greater activity than that of carbonate or oxid of zine and of chromium (obtained according to the metli-
ods described by Patart and by “ Badische Soda und Anilin Fab.”) which is ordinarily considered to be one of the best catalyzers.
Quantitative comparisons show that with

props.statement: Quantitative comparisons under the same catalytic space, temperature and gas velocity show that mineral smithsonite has an enormously greater activity than carbonate or oxide of zinc and chromium made by the Patart and Badische methods, ordinarily considered one of the best catalysts.

props.name: compact, no local overheating; activity not lessened with unpurified gases

evidence.quote: The present catalyzer, due to its compact- ness, possesses the advantageous property of not being subject to localized overheating, and of having a peculiar stability; and even
sfter a prolonged operation with unpurified gases, its catalytic activity is not lessened in the.slightest.

props.statement: Owing to its compactness the catalyst is not subject to localized overheating and has a peculiar stability; even after prolonged operation with unpurified gases its activity is not lessened in the slightest.
